title: Sally Rooney’s books no longer sold in UK over support for banned pro-Palestinian group | CNN
text:
Source: Reuters

Irish novelistSally Rooney’sbooks will no longer be sold in Britain over her plans to use her royalties to support Palestine ​Action, a pro-Palestinian group banned as a terrorist organisation, Rooney and ‌her publisher said on Wednesday.

The bestselling author, known for novels including “Normal People” and “Conversations with Friends,” has been a vocal supporter ofPalestine Action, including after it was proscribed by ​the British government under terrorism laws last year.

Rooney previously said in ​a witness statement submitted to London’s High Court, in support of ⁠a legal challenge over the ban on Palestine Action, that her plans ​could lead to her books being withdrawn from sale in Britain.

Her publisher Faber ​said on Wednesday that it had agreed with Rooney that “we can no longer supply her works in the UK in any format,” though it would sell her works elsewhere.

“Current ​legislation in the UK has led to circumstances where Faber cannot pass ​on UK earnings to Sally Rooney for her work,” Faber said in a statement.

“To sell ‌a ⁠writer’s work and not be able to pass on earnings is an unconscionable situation for a publisher.”

Rooney said in a statement: “I have made every effort to be honest with the public about my beliefs and intentions and I ​am wholly prepared to ​accept the ⁠consequences.”

Palestine Action, which had increasingly targeted Israel-linked defense companies, was banned shortly after a June 2025 break-in at the ​Royal Air Force’s Brize Norton base.

Last year, Palestine Action’s co-founder ​Huda Ammori ⁠challenged the ban and the High Courtruled in her favorin February, before the Court of Appealoverturned that decisionin June. The Supreme Court is due ⁠to ​hear an appeal next month.

More than 3,000 people ​have since been arrested for holding signs in support of Palestine Action and its proscription has ​been criticized by civil liberties groups.
